rationale.conceptual: The method is a routine DFT slab model with PBE functional, TS dispersion, and standard free energy corrections. It is a systematic application of known computational chemistry protocols; no custom algorithm or deep theory derivation is required.
rationale.execution: The workflow involves constructing undoped and doped models, screening doping sites, optimizing multiple intermediates, and computing zero-point energies and entropies. This is a multi-stage pipeline (~4-5 stages) with dependencies, but the tools (DFT code, scripting) are standard.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard DFT slab calculations with well-established functionals to study ORR on doped Co–gN₄ catalysts. The conceptual challenge is understanding and correctly applying an existing computational protocol; the execution requires a multi-step pipeline of structure building, geometry optimizations, and free energy calculations, but no novel methods or extreme resources.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Plane-wave DFT on ~100-atom slabs with moderate k-point meshes can run on a multi-core CPU; typical RAM demand is 16–32 GB. No large external datasets are needed.
